fit.mekko_time: The rows are years. A Mekko compares size and mix at one point; with years as widths they get re-sorted by size and the flow of time is lost.
fit.line_not_time: The rows are not time periods. A line implies a flow over time, so connecting separate items can mislead.
fit.non_additive_stack: The unit is “{unit}”. Rates, averages and indices cannot be added up, so stacked or share charts do not fit.
fit.many_columns: There are {n} items. Their names will be hard to read in a column chart.
fit.many_lines: There are {n} lines — too many to read. Highlight one, or narrow the rows and columns shown.
fit.negative_share: Some values are negative. A 100% share chart cannot show negative values.
fit.heading: How this data fits the chart
field.dimensionsHint: Used for the table’s corner heading and for legend and table headings (e.g. rows = year, columns = region).
needs.DRIVER_BRIDGE: First row = start, last row = end, rows in between = drivers (first column)
needs.BUBBLE: Rows = items × column 1 = X, column 2 = Y (column 3 = size)
fit.bridge_one_col: Driver charts use only the first column ({col}): first row = start, last row = end, rows between = drivers.
fit.relation_cols: Relationship charts read column 1 as X and column 2 as Y (and column 3 as size for bubbles). Add at least two numeric columns.

suggest.heading: With this data, you could also
suggest.items_two_metrics: Each item has two numeric measures. To show how they relate or where items sit, a scatter plot fits.
suggest.items_three_metrics: Each item has three numeric measures. To add size to a relationship, a bubble chart fits (column 1 = X, 2 = Y, 3 = size).
suggest.single_col_changes: One column mixes positive and negative values. For drivers from a start to an end value, a waterfall fits.
suggest.years_rows: The rows are years. To show change over time, a line chart fits.
fit.relation_years: The columns are years. Scatter and bubble charts use two or three measures per item (e.g. growth, margin, sales) as X, Y and size. For change over years, a line chart fits.

privacy.title: How we handle your data (beta)
privacy.lead: Where the data and requests you enter in Biz Slide Coach are stored, what they are used for, and what they are not used for.
privacy.point1: Your data (table values) is stored only in your account. It is never sent to the AI and never used to train AI.
privacy.point2: Only your request text is sent to the AI. It is sent with storage turned off at the provider (OpenAI API), and is not used for training.
privacy.point3: In normal operation, we do not look at individual users’ data or requests.
privacy.data.title: Your data and slides
privacy.data.1: Table data and slide content (title, source, etc.) are saved in your account. Other users cannot see them.
privacy.data.2: Table data is not sent to the AI and not used to train AI.
privacy.data.3: PowerPoint files are built in your browser and are not stored on our servers.
privacy.data.4: You can delete saved charts from My charts at any time.
privacy.consult.title: Requests (describe what you want to say)
privacy.consult.1: Only the request text is sent to the AI (OpenAI API) to suggest angles, with storage turned off at OpenAI. OpenAI does not use API data to train its models.
privacy.consult.2: While logged in, your requests are kept in “Request history” on My charts (only you can see and delete them).
privacy.consult.3: When the AI is unavailable, the app reads your request with built-in rules (nothing is sent out).
privacy.operator.title: Access by the operator
privacy.operator.1: In normal operation, the operator does not look at individual data, slides or requests.
privacy.operator.2: If access is ever needed (e.g. to investigate a bug), we will ask for your consent first.
privacy.improve.title: What we use to improve the service
privacy.improve.1: Information that contains no data, request text or messages, such as which entry, angle or chart was chosen and which screens were viewed, may be used to improve and develop the service.
privacy.improve.2: When you send 👍 / 👎 on suggestions, the operator reviews that request, the suggestions (angles and picks) and your comment to improve the suggestions. Table data is not included.
privacy.improve.3: Messages sent via “Feedback” are read by the operator and used for improvement.
privacy.account.title: Email address
privacy.account.1: Used only for login and, if you opted in, important announcements.
privacy.account.2: We never sell or give it to third parties.

order.segmentText: Sets one order for the segments ({seg}) across the whole chart: stacking, legend and color order follow it. Descending / ascending compare each segment's total across all categories ({cat}). Each bar is not sorted on its own, so every bar uses the same order. Sheet / reverse keep or flip the order in your table. “Others” always stays last.
order.segmentLegacy: (If you have not chosen one, segments follow the largest share in the last bar.)
order.categoryText: Sets the order of the categories ({cat}, along the axis). Descending / ascending compare each category's total across all segments ({seg}), i.e. the height of the whole bar. Segment order does not change. Sheet / reverse keep or flip the order in your table. “Others” always stays last. Not available when the axis is years or periods.
order.categoryTextMekko: Sets the order of the Mekko columns ({cat}). Descending / ascending compare each column's total (its width = size). The segments ({seg}) inside each column keep their order (set that with segment order). “Others” always stays last.
check.headOk: Checked your data: {rows} items × {cols} series, {numbers} numbers. Nothing looks off. You're good to go.
check.headIssues: Checked your data: {rows} items × {cols} series, {numbers} numbers. {n} things are worth a look. You can go ahead without fixing them, but it's safer to check.
check.headError: Some of this can't make a correct chart yet. Fix it as described below, then paste again.
check.foot: You can still edit any cell after inserting.
check.empty: No table found. Select the range in Excel, copy it, and paste it here.
check.tooLarge: {rows} rows is too large to read (up to {maxRows} rows and {maxCols} columns). Paste only the range the chart needs; a slide usually lands better with the top items or totals.
check.noTable: Couldn't read this as a table. Try a layout with column names in the first row and item names in the first column.
check.noNumbers: No numbers could be read. Check that number columns aren't text (e.g. “about 100”).
check.inCellBreaks: Turned {n} line breaks inside cells into spaces.
check.titleRows: “{text}” above the table looks like a title, so it's left out of the data. Your message works best in the slide's message title.
check.noteRows: “{text}” below the table looks like a note or source, so it's left out of the data. Put the source in the slide's Source field to show it neatly at the bottom.
check.european: These look like European-format numbers (1.234,5). Read that way, 1.234,5 becomes 1234.5 and 2.000 becomes 2000.
check.totalRows: The “{names}” row looks like a total. Stacked charts and Mekko would count it twice, so leaving it out is recommended (the chart can show totals itself).
check.totalCols: The “{names}” column looks like a total. As a series it would be counted twice, so leaving it out is recommended.
check.unreadable: {n} cells can't be read as numbers (e.g. “{sample}”). They are left blank, not 0. Turn them into numbers to include them.
check.excelErrors: {n} Excel errors (e.g. {sample}). They are left blank. Fixing the formula in Excel and pasting again is the safest.
check.missing: {n} cells such as “{sample}” mark missing values; they are read as blank (not 0).
check.negatives: Read {n} cells such as “{sample}” as negative (▲ or parentheses).
check.percentMix: The “{col}” column mixes “{pct}” and “{dec}”. {dec} is read as {as} so the column compares as %.
check.unitMix: Units are mixed ({units}). They are aligned to “{to}” so they compare correctly.
check.unitConflict: Different kinds of units ({units}) are in one table. They can't share an axis, so a separate slide per unit is recommended.
check.unitPartial: Some numbers have “{unit}” and some have no unit. Check that the unitless ones use the same unit.
check.dupRows: Several items share a name ({names}). They are kept separate, not added up. To combine them, total them in Excel first.
check.dupCols: Several columns share a name ({names}). The legend can't tell them apart, so renaming them is recommended.
check.large: A large table ({rows} items × {cols} series). It works, but a slide shows about 10 at most; try “Show top only”.
check.outlier: “{sample}” is over 1000× larger than the other values. Check for a digit or unit slip.
check.unitRead: Read the unit as “{unit}”. It goes into the chart's unit.
check.gridUnreadable: {n} pasted cells couldn't be read as numbers and were left blank (e.g. “{sample}”), not 0. Turn them into numbers to include them.
guard.messageDraft: “{name}” has unsaved changes. What would you like to do before starting something new?
guard.draftAndGo: Keep as a draft and start new
guard.draftNote: Drafts can be opened any time from Drafts in My charts (kept in your account, so any computer works).
draft.missing: That draft wasn't found (it was deleted, or belongs to another account or browser).
draft.head: Unsaved drafts ({n})
draft.note: Unsaved work kept in this browser only (latest 5, for 30 days). Sign in to keep drafts in your account and open them on any computer.
check.mixedSum: “{a}” and “{b}” are different kinds of measures (units), so adding them up in a {chart} makes the total meaningless. Leaving “{b}” out is recommended. To show the rate too, switch to Column + Line or a scatter after inserting.
check.unitSync: The pasted table is in “{to}”, but the slide's unit is “{from}”. The slide unit will change to “{to}”.
check.opt.unitSync: Match the slide unit to the table (untick to keep “{from}”)
check.staleMeta: This replaces the data entirely. The source “{source}” and period “{period}” may belong to the old data; check them in the Slide section after inserting.
meaning.heading: Does the chart make sense?
meaning.errorLead: As it stands, the numbers won't mean what they appear to.
meaning.fix.autofixEnd: Set the end to the calculated value
meaning.mixed_sum: “{a}” and “{b}” use different units (kinds of measure), so a {chart} can't add them up; the totals and shares shown are meaningless. Use one measure, or a chart that shows the two side by side.
meaning.mixed_currency: Series in different currencies ({list}) share one axis. Convert them to one currency, or give each currency its own slide.
meaning.mixed_axis: Rates ({rates}) share an axis with amounts or counts. The scales don't match; put rates on a right axis (Column + Line) or leave them out.
meaning.unit_mismatch: The slide unit is “{unit}”, but the column “{col}” is in “{colUnit}”. The numbers would appear with the wrong unit. Make the units match.
meaning.zero_total: “{rows}” totals 0, so its mix can't be drawn (it's left out of the chart).
meaning.bridge_mismatch: Start {start} plus the changes is {calc}, but the end is {end} (gap {diff}). The gap is drawn as an “Adjustment” bar. Check for a typo.
meaning.bridge_subtotals: Subtotals or totals ({rows}) sit in the middle. A waterfall adds them as changes and double-counts. Remove them or use another slide.
meaning.bubble_size: Some bubble sizes ({col}) are 0, negative or blank ({rows}). Size is shown as area, so these can't be drawn correctly.
meaning.cagr_start: Series with a value of 0 or less in {from} ({cols}) have no CAGR (shown as “—”).
meaning.year_gap: There are gaps between years. CAGR uses the actual span {from}→{to} ({years} years).
meaning.fiscal_mix: Calendar years ({cal}) and fiscal years ({fy}) are mixed. Check that the periods have the same length.
title.staleText: The data changed after you wrote this title. Check that its claim (numbers, ranking, change) still matches the chart.
meaning.confirmLead: These slides may give the wrong impression as they stand.
meaning.confirmTail: Export anyway? (Cancelling doesn't use an export.)
meaning.bridge_fixed: The entered end is {end}, but it is drawn as start + changes = {calc} (gap {diff}).
meaning.blocked: Saving, export and sending are paused because a slide's numbers don't add up meaningfully. Fix it from the red note above the preview, or choose “I understand, use as is”.
meaning.blockedOther: Other slides ({list}) also have numbers that don't add up meaningfully. Saving and export stay paused until they're fixed.
meaning.override: I understand; use as is (allow save and export)
meaning.overridden: Using as is. We'll check again if the content changes.
convert.need_metrics: {chart} needs {n} number columns (you have {have}). Add columns or show more in the data section.
convert.family_in_use: Another slide uses {chart}-shaped data, so this slide's data can't replace it. Duplicate the slide first, or edit the data.
convert.data_changed: Not changed, because the data would have changed (the chart stays as it was).
convert.render: Couldn't draw it as {chart}, so nothing changed.
error.panel: This section couldn't be shown. Your data is safe. Undo, or try showing it again (if it keeps happening, please send feedback).
meaning.fix.clearUnit: Clear the unit (show units in the axis names)
meaning.axis_unit_mismatch: The slide shows the unit “{unit}”, but the axis “{col}” is in “{colUnit}”. The numbers would appear with the wrong unit. Clear the unit and show it in the axis names, or make the units match.
draft.empty: No drafts. Use “Keep as draft” in the editor, or “Keep as a draft and start new”, to put work here.
draft.current: Being edited in this browser (not kept yet) · {n} slides
discard.title: Discard unsaved work?

discard.revertTitle: Revert to the last saved version?

guard.draftNoteLocal: Drafts can be opened from Drafts in My charts (you're not signed in, so they stay in this browser only: latest 5, for 30 days).
draft.noteRemote: Work not yet saved as a chart. It's kept in your account, so you can open it on any computer. When it's ready, open it and Save to move it to Charts.
draft.moved: Moved {n} drafts from this browser to your account.
draft.saved: Kept as a draft (Drafts in My charts)
draft.localOnly: You're not signed in, so drafts stay in this browser only.
save.status.draft: Draft (not saved as a chart yet)
save.status.draftDirty: Changed since the draft was kept
discard.revertDraftBody: Changes since you kept the draft will be removed (Undo can bring them back).

side.head: Beside the chart (supporting view)
side.infoText: Places a view computed from the same data in the right third of the slide. Increase = each part's change from start to end (absolute; which parts contributed to the growth). Growth rate = each part's CAGR (how fast it grew). Colors match the main chart. It carries over when you switch charts, where possible.
side.block.no_absolute: Shares alone can't give increases or growth rates. Enter absolute values (amounts, counts) to use this.
side.block.no_cagr: CAGR needs years and positive start and end values.
side.block.one_series: Needs two or more parts to compare.
side.block.one_period: Needs two or more points in time.
side.overflow: {n} items on the right are hard to read (aim for {max} or fewer). Show only the top items, or stack the views.
side.deltaRank: Change since last time (on the same rows as the ranking)
side.cagrRank: Growth rate (CAGR) (on the same rows as the ranking)
side.metric2Rank: Second metric (on the same rows as the ranking)
side.metric2: Second metric (on the same rows as the ranking)
needs.secondMetric: two metric tables (left and right metric)
side.formHint.delta.bars: Sorted by increase, to show ranking and gaps.
side.formHint.delta.table: To check exact start, end and change values.
side.formHint.delta.waterfall: Shows how each part's change adds up to the change in the total.
side.formHint.cagr.bars: Compares growth rates by bar length, fastest first.
side.formBlock.not_parts: A waterfall only works when the parts make up the whole (an additive breakdown).
side.formBlock.not_reconciled: The total column doesn't match the sum of the parts, so a waterfall isn't available (check the totals in your data).
side.formHint.delta.numbers: No bars — just the figures, aligned to the rows on the left. Readable even with many items.
side.formHint.cagr.numbers: No bars — just the figures, aligned to the rows on the left. Readable even with many items.
side.formHint.metric2.numbers: No bars — just the figures, aligned to the rows on the left. Readable even with many items.
side.formHint.metric2.bars: Shows the second metric as bars on its own axis.
side.formHint.rank.bars: Shown as bars on the same rows as the ranking.
side.coach.notParts: These items are not parts of one whole (rates or 'of which' items are mixed in). Read the right side as changes by item, not as contributions to the total.
side.coach.mismatch: The '{name}' column doesn't match the sum of the items: {rows}. Check how the total is defined (are any items missing?).
side.coach.noCagr: CAGR can't be computed for: {names} (start or end is zero or blank). They show as N/A.
side.toStacked: Stack them (items across the lower panel)

tpl.warn.nextNoOwner: Some actions have no owner or due date (no. {n}).
tpl.two.hint: Compare two things side by side. Headings are free text (as-is / to-be, before / after, option A / B).
tpl.two.label: {side} heading
tpl.bullet.hint: Enter one point per line (aim for seven or fewer). Add an optional one-line note under each.
tpl.bullet.textPlaceholder: e.g. Korea and Taiwan grew in both visitors and spending
tpl.bullet.subPlaceholder: e.g. Spending more than doubled vs 2019
tpl.warn.twoOneSide: Only one side has content (add what it is compared with).
tpl.warn.twoNoLabel: A side has no heading (make clear what is being compared).
tpl.warn.bulletMany: There are {n} lines (aim for {max} or fewer).
tpl.warn.bulletLong: Some lines are long (line {n}; aim for {max} characters).
tpl.warn.bulletSubLong: Some notes are long (line {n}; aim for {max} characters).
tpl.warn.bulletRefGone: The slide referenced by line {n} no longer exists.
tpl.warn.numRefGone: The slide referenced by number {n} no longer exists.
tpl.basic.pasteHint: Copy from Excel or another table and paste into a cell (fills right and down from that cell). The first row is treated as headings.
tpl.basic.headerRow: Treat the first row as headings
tpl.basic.headerCol: Treat the first column as row headings
tpl.warn.fmtNoNumber: “{name}” has a number format but no cells that read as numbers (for dates or names, clear the format).
tpl.switch.title: Switch to “{to}”. What should it contain?
tpl.switch.body: The “{from}” content is kept, so you can switch back later.
tpl.switch.convertNote: Copies item names, current values and comparison values (in tables: 1st column = item, 2nd = current, 3rd = comparison).
tpl.switch.previous: Restore what you entered in “{to}” before
tpl.switch.previousNote: Uses the content you entered in this type earlier.
tpl.switch.sampleNote: Starts again from an empty sample.
tpl.fromConsultation: These values were read from your request. Please check they are right.
grid.pickNote: Tick the rows and columns to delete.
grid.pickKeep: At least two rows and two columns are kept.
data.detachShort: Use separate data for this slide
tpl.exec.draftNeedMsg: The other slides’ messages (titles) are still samples. Write them and this button becomes available.
tpl.exec.draftAllFilled: Every item already has text (the draft only fills empty items).
tpl.exec.draftNoMatch: No slide messages match the empty items.
tpl.exec.coachLast: The executive summary is best written last. Write the other slides’ messages (titles) first, then draft it here ({n}/{total} done).
story.sampleAsk: This chart still uses sample data. Do you want to enter your past data?
tpl.table.rateCell: Rating at row {r}, column {c}: {v} (click for next)
scope.dataNone: Not in your request (the chart would start with sample data)
scope.dataPasteLabel: Paste a table copied from Excel (years or items in the first row, names in the first column).
scope.dataBad: Couldn’t read this as a table. Paste a tab-separated table (an Excel copy).
scope.dataLater: Start with sample data, add mine later
scope.dataLaterNote: Starts with sample data. You can paste yours later from the editor.
